content.text:
Fixed in `lib/request.js:259` — the `port` getter now parses from `this.host` instead of reading `this.headers.host ?? this.headers[':authority']` directly:

```js
port: {
  get () {
    const portReg = /(?<port>:\d+)$/
    const matches = portReg.exec(this.host)
    ...
```

Because `buildRequestWithTrustProxy` overrides the `host` getter on its own prototype, `this.host` resolves to the trust-proxy variant when `trustProxy` is on, so `host`, `hostname` and `port` all read the same effective source again (`x-forwarded-host` when trusted, otherwise `host`, then `:authority`). The `#6603` parsing logic — regex anchored at the end, IPv6 safe, `null` when absent — is unchanged.

Coverage added in `test/request-port.test.js`: a trust-proxy case set built with `buildRequest(Request, true)` covering the port from `x-forwarded-host`, the last entry of a multi-value `x-forwarded-host`, an IPv6 forwarded host, a forwarded host with no port, fallback to `host`, fallback to `:authority`, and no host headers at all — each also asserting `host`/`hostname`/`port` agree. That file passes (2/2); I did not run the wider suite.

Per the repo's risk map notes:
- **Co-change partner `lib/reply.js`**: opened; it has no reference to `port` or `host` (it touches request state only via `kRouteContext`/`kRequestSignal`/`kTimeoutTimer`), so it did not need a change.
- **Two-variant prototype construction preserved**: the change is confined to the base prototype's getter; the trust-proxy path and its `kHasBeenDecorated` flag are untouched.
- **Docs**: `docs/Reference/Request.md:31` already documents `port` as "parsed from `request.host`", so the code now matches the docs — no doc edit needed.

One note: this is a behavior change for anyone relying on the post-`#6603` semantics of `port` always reflecting the literal `Host` header under `trustProxy`; they now get the forwarded port. That's the intent of the issue, and it matches the documented contract.
